quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: The rate at which employees leave a company and are replaced.
The strategic process of finding and attracting skilled employees.
A measurable value showing how well a goal or objective is being achieved.
The formal process employees use to raise workplace complaints.

quests.hint: Every one of these phrases connects to how a company manages and evaluates its employees.
quests.explanation: Turnover rate measures how often employees leave, and talent acquisition is the effort to bring new ones in to replace them. Performance indicator tracks how well anyone is doing their job, and grievance procedure is different from the other three — the formal path an employee follows to raise a complaint.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: A detailed document listing a person's education, experience, and achievements.
A brief letter sent with a job application explaining why you are suitable.
An assessment used to measure a person's natural ability for a type of work.
A reduced list of the best candidates chosen from a larger group.

quests.hint: Notice how each phrase connects to a different stage of applying for a job.
quests.explanation: A curriculum vitae lists your background in detail, and a cover letter is sent alongside it, explaining why you're a good fit. An aptitude test may follow, measuring natural ability, and shortlist is different from the other three — the smaller group of candidates chosen to move forward.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: A path or road chosen for the beautiful views it offers rather than speed.
A well-known or important feature that helps identify a location.
A small town that has developed primarily to serve tourists.
A period when a destination has fewer visitors, often with lower prices.

quests.hint: These phrases all tie back to planning a relaxing trip somewhere new.
quests.explanation: A scenic route is chosen for its views rather than speed, and a landmark is often what makes those views worth seeing. Resort town describes the kind of destination built around tourism, and off-season is different from the other three — it's about timing, not location.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Living together in the same home, especially without being married.
The state of having become distant from someone who was close.
The family of your husband or wife.
Describing a family or group with strong, caring connections between members.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase describes a different kind of closeness, or distance, within a family.
quests.explanation: Cohabitation describes living together, often without marriage, while estrangement describes the opposite kind of distance — a relationship that has broken down. In-laws are a specific set of relatives gained through marriage, and close-knit is different from the other three — it describes how tightly connected a family feels, not a specific relationship or living arrangement.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: The legal protections that apply when a person buys goods or services.
Describing a product made to look genuine but is actually a fake copy.
When a company asks customers to return a product due to a safety issue.
The period of time during which a customer can return a purchased item.

quests.hint: Each of these phrases points to protecting shoppers when something goes wrong with a purchase.
quests.explanation: Consumer rights are the legal protections behind any purchase, and a product recall is one situation where those rights matter most, when a product turns out to be unsafe. Counterfeit describes a fake version of a genuine product, and return window is different from the other three — simply the time allowed to bring an item back, whether or not anything is wrong with it.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: A style of cooking that combines ingredients and techniques from different cultures.
A substance in food that can trigger an allergic reaction.
A restaurant menu offering many small dishes to sample a chef's range.
A person's ability to taste and appreciate different flavors.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to the experience of eating at a creative restaurant.
quests.explanation: Fusion cuisine blends styles from different cultures, and a tasting menu is often the best way to sample a chef's full range of it. Allergen is a safety concern to watch for in any dish, and palate is different from the other three — it describes a person's own sense of taste, not a feature of the food itself.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: A new version of a program, often improving performance or fixing problems.
The ability of two devices or programs to work together properly.
The original settings a device or program uses unless changed by the user.
To identify and fix the cause of a technical problem.

quests.hint: Each phrase relates to keeping a device or program running smoothly.
quests.explanation: A software update improves a program over time, and compatibility determines whether it will even work properly with your device. Default settings are what you start with before making any changes, and troubleshoot is different from the other three — it's the action you take once something has actually gone wrong.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Treating the whole person, including mental and social factors, not just symptoms.
Medical treatment aimed at preventing illness before it occurs.
Medical care focused on relieving symptoms rather than curing a disease.
A patient's agreement to medical treatment after being fully informed of the risks.

quests.hint: Each phrase ties back to a different philosophy or approach within healthcare.
quests.explanation: Preventative care aims to stop illness before it starts, while palliative care takes the opposite approach, focusing on comfort once a disease can't be cured. Holistic care considers the whole person, not just the illness, and informed consent is different from the other three — it's a patient's agreement, not a type of treatment.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: The final practice of a performance with full costumes and staging.
The place where a concert, event, or performance takes place.
When an audience stands up and claps to show great appreciation for a performance.
The full set of pieces a performer or company is prepared to perform.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to putting on and experiencing a live performance.
quests.explanation: A dress rehearsal happens just before opening night, and a venue is simply where that night takes place. Repertoire is the full range of works a performer is ready to present, and standing ovation is different from the other three — it's the audience's own reaction, given only if the performance truly impresses them.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: A short trip taken to perform a specific small task.
Preparing large amounts of food at one time to be eaten over several days.
The process of removing unnecessary items from a living space.
A home fitted with internet-connected devices that can be controlled remotely.

quests.hint: Every one of these phrases connects to managing everyday tasks around the house.
quests.explanation: An errand is a quick trip to complete a small task, while batch cooking saves time by preparing several meals at once. Decluttering is a different kind of task, clearing unwanted items from a space, and smart home is different from all three — it's about technology, not a task you personally do.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: An official document showing a student's grades and progress.
A test given and scored the same way for all students, used to compare performance.
A small group of students who meet to review material together.
A staff member who helps students plan their courses and goals.

quests.hint: Notice how each phrase connects to a student's experience of school, from grades to guidance.
quests.explanation: A report card shows a student's grades, and a standardized test is one common way those grades get measured, using the same test for everyone. A study group helps students prepare together, and academic advisor is different from the other three — a staff member who helps plan a student's path, not a test or a document.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: A meeting conducted by telephone or video link between people in different places.
A list of items to be discussed or dealt with at a meeting.
The official written record of what was said and decided at a meeting.
A specific task agreed upon at a meeting that must be completed.

quests.hint: These phrases all tie back to a different part of running an effective meeting.
quests.explanation: An agenda is prepared before a meeting, listing what will be discussed, whether in person or by teleconference. Minutes are written during or after the meeting, recording what was decided, and action point is different from the other three — a specific task someone agrees to complete afterward.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Walking long distances, usually over rough or mountainous terrain.
Wild, natural land that has not been developed by humans.
A form of travel focused on experiencing nature without harming it.
A large protected area where wild animals live and can be observed.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to exploring nature responsibly.
quests.explanation: Trekking is the physical activity of walking long distances through rough land, and wilderness is the kind of natural land you'd be walking through. Eco-tourism is a broader philosophy of traveling without causing harm, and game reserve is different from the other three — a specific, protected place where wild animals can be observed.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: An object passed down through generations within a family.
Money, property, or possessions received from someone after they die.
A person's closest living relative, often responsible for medical decisions.
A legal document stating a person's wishes regarding medical treatment if incapacitated.

quests.hint: Each of these phrases points to what a family passes down, and who makes decisions.
quests.explanation: An heirloom is a meaningful object passed down through a family, while inheritance is broader, covering any money or property received after someone dies. Next of kin identifies who that closest relative actually is, and living will is different from the other three — a legal document, not a person or a possession.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: Made to a specific customer's individual requirements; custom-made.
Describing something of high quality from a past era.
The amount of money an item can be sold for after initial purchase.
A document proving an item is genuine and not a fake.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to buying something rare, custom-made, or previously owned.
quests.explanation: Bespoke describes something made specifically for you, while vintage describes something valued simply for being from an earlier era. Resale value looks ahead to what an item might be worth later, and authenticity certificate is different from the other three — a document proving an item is genuine, not a quality of the item itself.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: To generate a large number of ideas freely, without immediately judging them.
A problem-solving approach that uses creative, indirect ways of reasoning.
The introduction of new ideas, methods, or products.
The repetition of a process with the aim of improving the outcome each time.

quests.hint: Each word relates to a different stage of coming up with and refining new ideas.
quests.explanation: To brainstorm is to generate many ideas quickly, without judging them yet, and lateral thinking is one creative approach that can help. Innovation is often the result, a genuinely new idea or method, and iteration is different from the other three — the process of repeating and improving something that already exists.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: The fee a patient pays when collecting medicine prescribed by a doctor.
A study that tests new medicines or treatments on people.
An online tool that suggests possible conditions based on symptoms entered.
A complete file of a patient's health history and treatments.

quests.hint: Each phrase relates to a different part of the modern healthcare system.
quests.explanation: Prescription charges are paid when collecting medicine, while a clinical trial happens much earlier, testing whether a medicine works at all. A symptom checker is a tool patients might use before even seeing a doctor, and medical record is different from the other three — the ongoing file of a patient's full health history.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: Software designed to help groups of people work together online.
A file that multiple people can view or edit together online.
The process of organizing, tracking, and prioritizing work to be done.
A brief, informal meeting where a team quickly checks in or plans next steps.

quests.hint: Each phrase ties back to how a modern team organizes and communicates about work.
quests.explanation: A collaboration tool is software built to help a team work together, and a shared document is one common example of it in action. Task management keeps track of what still needs to be done, and team huddle is different from the other three — a quick, informal meeting, not a tool or a document.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: The legal protections available to people who rent a property.
When a tenant rents all or part of their property to another person.
The legal process of removing a tenant from a property.
The process of extending a rental agreement for another term.

quests.hint: Every one of these phrases connects to the legal side of renting a home.
quests.explanation: Tenant rights protect renters throughout their time in a property, and lease renewal is a positive step within that time, extending the agreement. Subletting lets a tenant rent the space to someone else, and eviction is different from the other three — the legal removal of a tenant, usually the outcome no one wants.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A long walk in the countryside or on natural terrain.
A holiday taken on a large ship that stops at various destinations.
A non-scheduled flight hired privately rather than through a regular airline.
A pre-arranged holiday where transport, accommodation, and often food are included.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase describes a different style of vacation.
quests.explanation: A hike focuses on walking through nature, while a cruise focuses on traveling by sea, stopping at several destinations. A charter flight is booked privately rather than through a regular airline, and package holiday is different from the other three — a full trip bundled together, transport, stay, and often food included.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: Assessing a person's financial situation to determine if they qualify for support.
Money paid by the government to a person who has lost their job.
A place where free food is distributed to people who cannot afford to buy it.
Government programs designed to support people facing financial hardship.

quests.hint: Notice how each phrase connects to how a society supports people during hard financial times.
quests.explanation: Means testing checks a person's finances to see if they qualify for help, and unemployment benefit is one form of help they might then receive. A food bank offers a very direct, practical kind of support, and social safety net is different from the other three — the broad system of programs that all of this support belongs to.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A speaker's or writer's choice of words and clarity of pronunciation.
The rise and fall of a speaker's voice to convey meaning or emotion.
The ability to speak or write a language smoothly and with ease.
The quality of a text or speech being logically connected and easy to follow.

quests.hint: Each word describes a different quality of strong spoken or written English.
quests.explanation: Diction is about word choice and clear pronunciation, while intonation is about the rise and fall of your voice as you speak. Fluency measures how smoothly you communicate overall, and coherence is different from the other three — it's about how logically your ideas connect, in speech or in writing.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: A basic food that forms a large part of the diet in a particular region.
A rare or expensive food considered a special treat in a particular culture.
A small dish served before the main meal.
A sweet dish served at the end of a meal.

quests.hint: Each phrase names a different course or category of food on a menu.
quests.explanation: A staple food is eaten regularly as a basic part of the diet, while a delicacy is the opposite — rare and special, not eaten every day. An appetizer comes at the very start of a meal, and dessert is different from the other three — it's saved for the very end.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: The act of reporting illegal or unethical behavior within an organization to authorities.
A set of rules describing expected behavior within an organization.
A thorough investigation done before making a business decision.
Legal responsibility for causing loss or harm to another party.

quests.hint: These phrases all tie back to honesty and responsibility inside an organization.
quests.explanation: A code of conduct sets out expected behavior in advance, and due diligence is a careful check made before a major decision. Whistleblowing happens when someone reports behavior that breaks rules like these, and liability is different from the other three — legal responsibility for harm, not a rule or a process.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: Buses, trains, and other transport systems available for anyone to use.
The process of improving a run-down part of a city through new construction or repair.
The basic physical systems that support a community, such as roads and utilities.
Traffic so heavy that vehicles move slowly or not at all.

quests.hint: Each of these phrases points to how a city moves and grows.
quests.explanation: Infrastructure is the basic system a city relies on, including roads and utilities, and public transportation is one important part of that system. Urban renewal describes improving a rundown area over time, and congestion is different from the other three — a problem that happens when roads become too crowded to move freely.

quests.instruction: Match each phrase with its meaning.

pairs.value: The ongoing process of controlling a long-term health condition.
An inactive substance given to patients in trials to compare against a real treatment.
An unintended reaction that occurs alongside the main effect of a medicine.
A period during which the symptoms of a disease are reduced or absent.

quests.hint: Each phrase relates to living with, or being treated for, a long-term illness.
quests.explanation: Chronic disease management is the ongoing work of controlling a long-term condition, and side effect is something that might complicate that work, an unwanted reaction to treatment. Placebo is used mainly in research, to test whether a treatment truly works, and remission is different from the other three — a hopeful period when symptoms fade, not a treatment or a reaction at all.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: The technique of making drawings or models appear to move in a film.
Artificial visual or sound effects created for use in a film or show.
The art of capturing images on film or video.
A person who performs dangerous actions in place of an actor.

quests.hint: Each word or phrase relates to the craft behind what you see on screen.
quests.explanation: Animation brings drawings or models to life, while special effects add artificial visuals or sounds to any kind of film. Cinematography is the art of capturing it all on camera, and stunt double is different from the other three — a real person, standing in for dangerous scenes.

quests.instruction: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.value: A labor market where short-term contracts and freelance work are common.
The likelihood that a person will keep their job without the risk of becoming unemployed.
A model combining time in the office with working from home.
A planned period of time away from work, often for travel, study, or family.

quests.hint: Each phrase ties back to how modern working life has changed.
quests.explanation: The gig economy relies on short-term and freelance work rather than steady jobs, which can affect job security, how confident someone feels about keeping their position. Hybrid working blends office and home, and career break is different from the other three — a planned pause from work altogether, often for travel or family.

quests.instruction: Match each term with its correct meaning.

pairs.value: An arrangement where students or professionals spend time in another country.
The disorientation felt when experiencing a very different culture for the first time.
A person who lives and works in a country other than their own.
The process of returning someone to their home country.

quests.hint: Every one of these phrases connects to living or studying in a country that isn't your own.
quests.explanation: An exchange program sends someone abroad, often to study, and culture shock is a common reaction once they arrive somewhere very different. Expatriate describes anyone living outside their home country long-term, and repatriation is different from the other three — the process of eventually returning home.

quests.instruction: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.value: A general rise in prices that reduces the purchasing power of money.
A period of significant economic decline lasting at least two consecutive quarters.
The amount of money needed to cover basic expenses like housing, food, and bills.
The lowest amount an employer is legally allowed to pay a worker per hour.

quests.hint: Notice how each phrase connects to how the wider economy affects a person's daily finances.
quests.explanation: Inflation causes prices to rise, which drives up the cost of living for everyone. A recession is a more serious decline across the whole economy, and minimum wage is different from the other three — a legal floor on pay, meant to help protect people from exactly these kinds of pressures.
